subproblems.title: Lower mass bound from a monotone weighted ratio whose limit density is at least 1
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Λ ρ σ θ : ℝ) (m : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), 1 ≤ θ → 0 < σ → σ < ρ → MonotoneOn (fun τ : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * τ) / τ ^ n) * m τ) (Ioo 0 ρ) → Tendsto (fun τ : ℝ => m τ / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (τ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (ENNReal.ofReal θ)) → ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-(Λ * σ))) * (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (σ ^ n)) ≤ m σ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: extracted from the parent's supplied proof of idtp_fons_cc_monotonicity_bounds, steps A3–A5. The same argument is used in step B1 with Λ = 0. It is the 'monotonicity gives a lower density bound' step of Simon 7.3.1/7.3.3 (chapter-07.txt lines 326–330 and 420–430).

Notation. ω := ω_n = unitBallVolume n = volume(B_1(0)) in Euclid n = ℝ^n, and ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal. For τ ∈ ℝ put
  f(τ) := ofReal(e^{Λτ}/τ^n)·m(τ),
  q(τ) := m(τ)/(ω·ofReal(τ^n)).
Hypotheses:
- 1 ≤ θ and 0 < σ < ρ;
- f is nondecreasing on (0, ρ): if a ≤ b are in (0, ρ), then f(a) ≤ f(b);
- q(τ) → ofReal θ in [0, ∞] along 𝓝[>]0.
All arithmetic is in [0, ∞] unless stated otherwise.

1. (0 < ω < ∞.) Volume on the finite-dimensional inner product space Euclid n is an additive Haar measure. So it is positive on nonempty open sets and finite on bounded subsets of the proper space Euclid n. The open unit ball B_1(0) is nonempty, open and bounded, so ω ≠ 0 (measure_ball_pos) and ω ≠ ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). No restriction on n is needed: for n = 0, Euclid 0 is a point and ω = 1. Also, for τ > 0 we have τ^n > 0, so ofReal(τ^n) is positive and finite.

2. (Factorization of f on (0, ∞).) Let τ > 0.
- Since τ^n > 0, ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos gives ofReal(e^{Λτ}/τ^n) = ofReal(e^{Λτ})/ofReal(τ^n).
- Since ω ≠ 0 and ω ≠ ∞, mul_div_assoc and then ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left give ω·q(τ) = (ω·m(τ))/(ω·ofReal(τ^n)) = m(τ)/ofReal(τ^n).
- Writing a/b = a·b⁻¹ and using commutativity and associativity in [0, ∞]: f(τ) = ofReal(e^{Λτ})·ofReal(τ^n)⁻¹·m(τ) = ofReal(e^{Λτ})·(ω·q(τ)).

3. (Limit of f at 0⁺.)
- The map τ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λτ}) is continuous on ℝ: it composes τ ↦ Λτ, Real.exp and the continuous map ENNReal.ofReal. So it tends to ofReal(e^{Λ·0}) = ofReal(1) = 1 as τ → 0, and also along 𝓝[>]0 ≤ 𝓝 0.
- By hypothesis q(τ) → ofReal θ along 𝓝[>]0. Since ω ≠ ∞, ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul gives ω·q(τ) → ω·ofReal θ.
- ENNReal.Tendsto.mul applies to these two limits because the first limit is 1, which is neither 0 nor ∞. It gives ofReal(e^{Λτ})·(ω·q(τ)) → 1·(ω·ofReal θ) = ω·ofReal θ along 𝓝[>]0.
- By step 2 this function equals f on (0, ∞), which belongs to 𝓝[>]0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Hence f(τ) → ω·ofReal θ as τ → 0⁺ (Tendsto.congr').

4. (Comparison by monotonicity.) Let τ ∈ (0, σ]. Then 0 < τ ≤ σ < ρ, so τ and σ both lie in (0, ρ) and τ ≤ σ. Since f is nondecreasing on (0, ρ), f(τ) ≤ f(σ). Because σ > 0, the interval (0, σ] belongs to 𝓝[>]0 (Ioc_mem_nhdsGT). So f(τ) ≤ f(σ) holds eventually along 𝓝[>]0, which is a nontrivial filter on ℝ (nhdsGT_neBot). By step 3 and le_of_tendsto, ω·ofReal θ ≤ f(σ).

5. (Use of θ ≥ 1.) From 1 ≤ θ we get 1 ≤ ofReal θ (ENNReal.one_le_ofReal). Hence
  ω = ω·1 ≤ ω·ofReal θ ≤ f(σ) = ofReal(e^{Λσ}/σ^n)·m(σ).

6. (Removing the weight.) Multiplication in [0, ∞] is monotone in each factor. Multiply the inequality ω ≤ f(σ) of step 5 on the right by ofReal(σ^n), then on the left by ofReal(e^{−(Λσ)}):
  ofReal(e^{−(Λσ)})·(ω·ofReal(σ^n)) ≤ ofReal(e^{−(Λσ)})·(ofReal(e^{Λσ}/σ^n)·m(σ)·ofReal(σ^n)).
The real numbers e^{−(Λσ)} and e^{−(Λσ)}·(e^{Λσ}/σ^n) are ≥ 0 because σ > 0. So two applications of ENNReal.ofReal_mul, together with commutativity, rewrite the right-hand side as
  ofReal(e^{−(Λσ)}·(e^{Λσ}/σ^n)·σ^n)·m(σ).
Finally e^{−(Λσ)} = (e^{Λσ})⁻¹ (Real.exp_neg), e^{Λσ} ≠ 0 and σ^n ≠ 0. So e^{−(Λσ)}·(e^{Λσ}/σ^n)·σ^n = 1, and the right-hand side equals ofReal(1)·m(σ) = 1·m(σ) = m(σ).

7. Therefore ofReal(e^{−(Λσ)})·(ω_n·ofReal(σ^n)) ≤ m(σ). ∎
proof_key_steps: 0 < ω_n < ∞ because volume on Euclid n is an additive Haar measure and the unit ball is nonempty, open and bounded. Also ofReal(τ^n) ∈ (0, ∞) for τ > 0.
For τ > 0, f(τ) = ofReal(e^{Λτ})·(ω_n·q(τ)), by ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos and ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left.
ofReal(e^{Λτ}) → 1 and ω_n·q(τ) → ω_n·ofReal θ, so f(τ) → ω_n·ofReal θ as τ → 0⁺ (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul, then congruence on (0, ∞)).
f(τ) ≤ f(σ) for τ ∈ (0, σ], and (0, σ] ∈ 𝓝[>]0, so ω_n·ofReal θ ≤ f(σ) by le_of_tendsto. θ ≥ 1 then gives ω_n ≤ f(σ).
Multiply by ofReal(e^{−(Λσ)})·ofReal(σ^n). The real factor e^{−(Λσ)}·(e^{Λσ}/σ^n)·σ^n equals 1, which gives ofReal(e^{−(Λσ)})·(ω_n·ofReal(σ^n)) ≤ m(σ).

subproblems.title: Total mass is 0 or ∞ for a measure on ℝ^P with Euclidean lower density bounds at its support points
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ n. Let μ be a measure on (the Borel σ-algebra of) ℝ^P = Euclid P, and let ω_n := unitBallVolume n, the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n. Assume: every w ∈ ℝ^P with μ(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0 satisfies ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) ≤ μ(B_ρ(w)) for every ρ > 0. Here B denotes the open ball and ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal. Then μ(ℝ^P) = 0 or μ(ℝ^P) = ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), 1 ≤ n → (∀ w : Euclid P, (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → μ (ball w ε) ≠ 0) → ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) ≤ μ (ball w ρ)) → μ univ = 0 ∨ μ univ = ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: extracted from the parent's supplied proof of idtp_fons_cc_monotonicity_bounds, step B2 (Simon 7.3.3, proof of 3.3: density bounds for members of 𝒯; chapter-07.txt lines 420–470).

Notation. ω := ω_n = unitBallVolume n = volume(B_1(0)) in Euclid n. B_r(x) is the open ball (ball x r), and ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal.
Hypotheses:
- 1 ≤ n;
- μ is a measure on (the Borel σ-algebra of) ℝ^P = Euclid P;
- (H): every w ∈ ℝ^P with μ(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0 satisfies ω·ofReal(ρ^n) ≤ μ(B_ρ(w)) for all ρ > 0.

1. (Case distinction.) Either
- Case 1: some w ∈ ℝ^P has μ(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0; or
- Case 2: every x ∈ ℝ^P has some ε_x > 0 with μ(B_{ε_x}(x)) = 0.
Case 2 is the negation of Case 1.

2. (Case 1: bound by the total mass.) Fix w as in Case 1. By (H), and since μ is monotone and B_ρ(w) ⊆ ℝ^P, we have ω·ofReal(ρ^n) ≤ μ(B_ρ(w)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) for every ρ > 0. Since {ρ : ρ > 0} ∈ atTop, this inequality holds eventually as ρ → ∞.

3. (Case 1: unbounded growth.)
- ω ≠ 0, because volume on Euclid n is an additive Haar measure and hence positive on the nonempty open ball B_1(0) (measure_ball_pos).
- Since n ≥ 1, n ≠ 0, so ρ^n → ∞ as ρ → ∞ (tendsto_pow_atTop).
- ENNReal.ofReal tends to ∞ at +∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal_atTop), so by composition ofReal(ρ^n) → ∞ in [0, ∞].
- ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul (side condition ∞ ≠ 0) gives ω·ofReal(ρ^n) → ω·∞, and ω·∞ = ∞ because ω ≠ 0 (ENNReal.mul_top).

4. (Case 1: conclusion.) The filter atTop on ℝ is nontrivial. Applying le_of_tendsto to the limit of step 3 and the eventual bound of step 2 gives ∞ ≤ μ(ℝ^P), so μ(ℝ^P) = ∞ (top_le_iff).

5. (Case 2: local nullity.) For each x ∈ ℝ^P pick ε_x > 0 with μ(B_{ε_x}(x)) = 0. Since ε_x > 0, B_{ε_x}(x) is a neighbourhood of x (ball_mem_nhds), i.e. it belongs to 𝓝 x = 𝓝[ℝ^P] x (nhdsWithin_univ). Euclid P is second countable. So measure_null_of_locally_null with s = ℝ^P applies (every point of s has a neighbourhood within s of μ-measure 0), and it gives μ(ℝ^P) = 0. Explicitly: by the Lindelöf property of the second-countable space ℝ^P, countably many of the balls B_{ε_x}(x) cover ℝ^P, and countable subadditivity gives μ(ℝ^P) = 0.

6. (Conclusion.) In Case 1, μ(ℝ^P) = ∞. In Case 2, μ(ℝ^P) = 0. Hence μ(ℝ^P) = 0 or μ(ℝ^P) = ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: Split on whether some point w has μ(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0.
If such a w exists: ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) ≤ μ(B_ρ(w)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) for all ρ > 0.
ω_n ≠ 0 (Haar measure of the unit ball) and n ≥ 1, so ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) → ∞ as ρ → ∞. Hence μ(ℝ^P) = ∞ by le_of_tendsto.
Otherwise every point has a μ-null open-ball neighbourhood, and second countability (measure_null_of_locally_null with s = univ) gives μ(ℝ^P) = 0.
